# `PIXterm` - *draw images in your ANSI terminal with true color*

**`PIXterm`** ***shows images directly in your terminal***, recreating the pixels through a combination of [ANSI character background color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Colors) and the [unicode lower half block element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements). If image has transparency, an optional matte color can be used for background. Also, you can specify a dithering mode; in which case, the image is rendered using block elements with different shades, or using standard ASCII characters in the same way. In dithering mode, the matte color is used to fill the background of the blocks or characters.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.

Fetching images from HTTP/HTTPS is supported too.

## Usage

```
pixterm [options] <image file or URL>
```

### Options

- `-version` - show PIXterm version
- `-credits` - show some love to contributors <3
- `-d <mode>` - dithering mode:
  - `0` - no dithering (default)
  - `1` - with blocks
  - `2` - with chars
- `-go` - output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image
- `-m <color>` - matte color for transparency or background (optional, hex format, default: 000000)
- `-nobg` - disable background color (optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)
- `-s <method>` - scale method:
  - `0` - resize (default)
  - `1` - fill
  - `2` - fit
- `-tr <rows>` - terminal rows (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)
- `-tc <columns>` - terminal columns (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)

## Requirements

Your terminal emulator must support *true color* in order to display image colors correctly. In addition, you must use a monospaced font that includes the lower half block unicode character: `▄ (U+2584)`. [Envy Code R](https://damieng.com/blog/2008/05/26/envy-code-r-preview-7-coding-font-released) is recommended. If you want to use the dithering mode with blocks, the font must also include the following unicode characters: `█ (U+2588)`, `▓ (U+2593)`, `▒ (U+2592)`, `░ (U+2591)`. The dithering mode with characters works with standard ASCII chars.

# `PIXterm` - *draw images in your ANSI terminal with true color*

**`PIXterm`** ***shows images directly in your terminal***, recreating the pixels through a combination of [ANSI character background color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Colors) and the [unicode lower half block element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements). If image has transparency, an optional matte color can be used for background. Also, you can specify a dithering mode; in which case, the image is rendered using block elements with different shades, or using standard ASCII characters in the same way. In dithering mode, the matte color is used to fill the background of the blocks or characters.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.

Fetching images from HTTP/HTTPS is supported too.

## Usage

```
pixterm [options] <image file or URL>
```

### Options

- `-version` - show PIXterm version
- `-credits` - show some love to contributors <3
- `-d <mode>` - dithering mode:
  - `0` - no dithering (default)
  - `1` - with blocks
  - `2` - with chars
- `-go` - output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image
- `-m <color>` - matte color for transparency or background (optional, hex format, default: 000000)
- `-nobg` - disable background color (optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)
- `-s <method>` - scale method:
  - `0` - resize (default)
  - `1` - fill
  - `2` - fit
- `-tr <rows>` - terminal rows (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)
- `-tc <columns>` - terminal columns (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)

## Requirements

Your terminal emulator must support *true color* in order to display image colors correctly. In addition, you must use a monospaced font that includes the lower half block unicode character: `▄ (U+2584)`. [Envy Code R](https://damieng.com/blog/2008/05/26/envy-code-r-preview-7-coding-font-released) is recommended. If you want to use the dithering mode with blocks, the font must also include the following unicode characters: `█ (U+2588)`, `▓ (U+2593)`, `▒ (U+2592)`, `░ (U+2591)`. The dithering mode with characters works with standard ASCII chars.

    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True)
    return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode

    out,err,rc=run(args)
    print("ARGS",args,"RC",rc,"STDOUT len",len(out),"STDERR len",len(err))

    open(f"/tmp/out_{'_'.join(args) or 'none'}.txt","wb").write(out)
    print(out.decode())
    print("STDERR:",err.decode())

# Check -unknown stderr vs stdout lengths
out,err,rc=run(["-unknown"])
print("unknown stdout len",len(out),"stderr len",len(err))
print("unknown STDERR:",err[:2000])
print("unknown STDOUT tail:",out[1000:])

# Check invalid flag value types
for args in [["-d","abc","x"],["-tr","abc","x"],["-tc","xyz","x"],["-m","zzz","x"],["-m","12345","x"],["-m","1234567","x"],["-m","#ff0000","x"],["-m","ff0000","nonexistent.png"]]:
    out,err,rc=run(args)
    print("ARGS",args,"RC",rc,"stdout len",len(out),"stderr:",err[:500])

import zlib, struct

def png(path, w, h, pixels, color_type=2):
    # pixels list of rows, each row list of tuples
    raw=b""
    for y in range(h):
        raw+=b"\x00"
        for x in range(w):
            p=pixels[y][x]
            raw+=bytes(p)
    def chunk(typ,data):
        c=struct.pack(">I",len(data))+typ+data
        c+=struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(typ+data) & 0xffffffff)
        return c
    ihdr=struct.pack(">IIBBBBB",w,h,8,color_type,0,0,0)
    data=b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"+chunk(b"IHDR",ihdr)+chunk(b"IDAT",zlib.compress(raw))+chunk(b"IEND",b"")
    open(path,"wb").write(data)

# 2x2: TL red, TR green, BL blue, BR white
png("/tmp/2x2.png",2,2,[[(255,0,0),(0,255,0)],[(0,0,255),(255,255,255)]])
# 4x4 gradient
pix=[[(x*80,y*80,128) for x in range(4)] for y in range(4)]
png("/tmp/4x4.png",4,4,pix)
# 1x1 red

def seq_dither(path,tc,tr):

def seq_normal(path,tc,tr):
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-tc",str(tc),"-tr",str(tr),path],capture_output=True)
    out=p.stdout.decode(); v=[]
    for line in out.strip().split("\n"):

        if cells: v.append(int(cells[0][0])); v.append(int(cells[0][3]))

    # header 8, IFD after pixels at offset 8+4=12

def sinc(x):
    if x==0: return 1.0
    return math.sin(math.pi*x)/(math.pi*x)

    if abs(x)>=3: return 0.0
    return sinc(x)*sinc(x/3)
def resize1d(src, M):
    N=len(src); out=[]
    scale=N/M
    for i in range(M):
        center=(i+0.5)*scale-0.5
        support=3*max(1.0,scale)  # if downscale, kernel scaled
        # weights over j
        total=0.0; val=0.0
        jmin=int(math.floor(center-support)); jmax=int(math.ceil(center+support))
        for j in range(jmin,jmax+1):

            w=lanczos3(arg)
            # edge handling: clamp index? or skip out of range pixels?
            jj=min(max(j,0),N-1)

import math
def sinc(x):

    for i in range(M):

        v=val/total if total else 0
        if clip_stage: v=max(0,min(255,v))

import math
exec(open('/tmp/kernel2.py').read().split("avg=")[0])
def resize_map(src,M,name,scale_kernel,align):
    N=len(src); out=[]; scale=N/M; factor=max(1.0,scale) if scale_kernel else 1.0; supp=SUPPORT[name]*factor
    for i in range(M):
        if align=="center": c=(i+0.5)*scale-0.5
        elif align=="corner": c=i*(N-1)/(M-1) if M>1 else 0
        elif align=="left": c=i*scale
        elif align=="right": c=(i+1)*scale-1
        tot=0;val=0
        for j in range(int(math.floor(c-supp)),int(math.ceil(c+supp))+1):
            if 0<=j<N:
                w=K(name,(j-c)/factor); tot+=w; val+=w*src[j]
        out.append(max(0,min(255,val/tot)) if tot else 0)
    return out
avg=[104.5,88,127.5,167,150.5,188,130,127.5,100,125]
obs=[107,99,127,156,148,185,127,123,100]
for name in SUPPORT:
 for sk in [True,False]:
  for align in ["center","corner","left","right"]:
    r=[round(x) for x in resize_map(avg,9,name,sk,align)]
    print(name,sk,align,r,"err",sum(abs(r[i]-obs[i]) for i in range(9)))

import subprocess,re,os,zlib,struct
def make(w,h):
    path=f"/tmp/custom_{w}x{h}.png"
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raw=b"".join([b"\x00"+b"\xff\x00\x00"*w for _ in range(h)])
        def chunk(t,d): return struct.pack(">I",len(d))+t+d+struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(t+d)&0xffffffff)
        open(path,"wb").write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"+chunk(b"IHDR",struct.pack(">IIBBBBB",w,h,8,2,0,0,0))+chunk(b"IDAT",zlib.compress(raw))+chunk(b"IEND",b""))
    return path
def dims(path,tc,tr,d):
    p=subprocess.run(["/tmp/origdir/executable","-tc",str(tc),"-tr",str(tr),"-s","2","-d",str(d),path],capture_output=True)

    lines=p.stdout.decode().strip().split("\n") if p.stdout.strip() else []
    w=[len(re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m","",l)) for l in lines]
    return f"{w[0] if w else 0}x{len(lines)}"
for iw in [5,6,7,9,10,11,13,15,17,25,33,50,99,101]:

import subprocess,re
def seq(path,tc,tr,bin="/tmp/origdir/executable",horizontal=True):
    p=subprocess.run([bin,"-tc",str(tc),"-tr",str(tr),"-s","1",path],capture_output=True)

    print(v)

import zlib,struct,subprocess,re
def png(path,w,h,pix):

    for y in range(h):
